name: mixer-conversion-iip3
description: Swept-two-tone conversion gain (power into 50 ohm, primary; voltage ratio, secondary), LO-to-RF leakage, and two-tone IIP3 extrapolated from the swept 1:3-slope region, for a single npn13G2 HBT active-mixer placeholder, via transient + coherent-bin FFT (low-side LO, 1 GHz IF per spec/target-spec.md's DRAFT LO-range row). Includes a one-tone floor control so the IM3 read carries a measured distance-above-floor.
claim: PLACEHOLDER, NOT SPEC EVIDENCE: this bench proves the swept transient/FFT conversion-gain, LO-leakage, and two-tone-IIP3 extraction methodology works end to end against the real npn13G2 model, across the full HBT process x temperature x supply PVT grid. It does NOT claim any DRAFT target-spec row (spec/target-spec.md) is met -- the DUT is a single-ended, single-transistor mixer (RF and LO summed at one base node), not the double-balanced Gilbert-cell topology row 9's DRAFT target assumes, so LO-to-RF isolation in particular is expected to be far worse than a balanced design would show. SSB noise figure is NOT measured by this bench at all -- see evidence.notes for why (ngspice has no periodic-noise analysis). IIP3 is extrapolated by intersecting two least-squares lines (fundamental ~1, IM3 ~3) fitted over a STATED swept-drive window, per spec/porting-plan.md S4.1, with a one-tone floor control bounding how far above the transient sampler's interpolation-error floor the IM3 read sits (issue #165); it is still a PLACEHOLDER-circuit number, not a row-9 claim. Re-point this tb.json's netlist at design/'s ratified schematic once issue #1's spec is ratified and a real topology exists in design/.
netlist_provenance: schematic (placeholder harness-exercising stub; no ratified schematic exists in design/ yet -- design/README.md is still empty -- so this is neither the ratified schematic deck nor ever taken through layout, hence the parenthetical per testbench.py's PROVENANCE_RULE)
analyses: * ---- issue #165 swept two-tone drive: DRIVELIST (V peak per tone), ascending.
* The TRACKED IM3 is the upper sideband 2*f2-f1-fLO = 1037.5 MHz (vim3hi): it is
* the dominant pair member at every swept drive AND the one whose measured
* local slope is the ideal ~3 (see evidence notes; the lower sideband's slope
* genuinely expands, 3.3->3.9, and is echoed as a diagnostic only).
* Table loop: first step unrolled so every LOCALSLOPE row has a real predecessor.
echo "SWEEPPOINT vrf=0.01 pin_dbm=$&pin pfund_dbm=$&pfund pim3_lo_962_dbm=$&pim3lo_db pim3_hi_1037_dbm=$&pim3 lo_rf_leak_dbm=$&pleak"
echo "SWEEPPOINT vrf=$drv pin_dbm=$&pin pfund_dbm=$&pfund pim3_lo_962_dbm=$&pim3lo_db pim3_hi_1037_dbm=$&pim3 lo_rf_leak_dbm=$&pleak"
* ---- fit loop over the STATED fit window (DRIVELIST minus its floor-marginal
* lowest step and its slope-departing highest step; see evidence notes).
echo "SWEEPPOINT vrf=$drv pin_dbm=$&pin pfund_dbm=$&pfund pim3_lo_962_dbm=$&pim3lo_db pim3_hi_1037_dbm=$&pim3 lo_rf_leak_dbm=$&pleak"
echo "FITPOINT vrf=$drv pin_dbm=$&pin pfund_dbm=$&pfund pim3_dbm=$&pim3 lo_rf_leak_dbm=$&pleak"
* ---- one-tone floor control: same window, top-of-fit drive, second tone
* zeroed; the SAME 1037.5 MHz bin now holds only sampler floor + spurious.
* ---- least-squares lines over the fit window; IIP3 = their intersection.

conversion_gain_db.description: Sensitivity floor only (NOT a spec-compliance check): proves the PVT grid genuinely perturbs the placeholder's conversion gain rather than silently simulating one corner for all requested points. Do not read this as 'meets the 8 dB DRAFT conversion-gain target' -- see the testbench claim above. Read at the top-of-fit drive step (see evidence notes).

slope_fund_db_per_db.description: The fit window's fundamental line must have slope ~1 (linear output vs input, dB-for-dB) at every PVT point -- porting-plan S4.1's swept-1:3-slope requirement, fundamental leg.

slope_im3_db_per_db.description: The fit window's IM3 line must have slope ~3 (third-order small-signal behaviour) at every PVT point -- porting-plan S4.1's swept-1:3-slope requirement, IM3 leg. A window that quietly contained a compressed or floor-contaminated point breaks one of these two checks.

fit_n.description: The regression must use exactly the stated 5-point fit window (DRIVELIST 0.014..0.056 step); guards a window-list/accumulator mismatch after a future deck edit.

pim3_fit_margin_db.description: The two-tone IM3 read at the top-of-fit drive must sit at least this far above the one-tone floor control at the same drive and window (issue #165's measured 'IM3 above floor' reference). A margin collapse means the readout is back on the transient sampler's interpolation-error floor and the extrapolated IIP3 is not a device number.

evidence.data_provenance: simulated (ngspice, real npn13G2 VBIC model, no PDK inductor model used anywhere in this fixture -- see notes)
notes: Two-tone plan: f1=19.4375 GHz, f2=19.4625 GHz (25 MHz spacing, centered on the Ka-band downlink DRAFT's 19.45 GHz), fLO=18.45 GHz (low-side, 1 GHz IF per spec/target-spec.md's DRAFT LO-range row). IF fundamentals at 987.5/1012.5 MHz, IM3 pair at 962.5/1037.5 MHz -- all exact integer multiples of 12.5 MHz by construction. Every transient in the deck records the same window: t=[20ns, 99.998779296875ns] -- 65536 = 2^16 samples at tstep=1.220703125 ps = 80ns/65536, so the DFT record length is exactly 80 ns = 1/12.5MHz; t<20ns is discarded as settle time so the FFT window is in periodic steady state. Issue #165 method: the deck steps the two-tone drive (foreach + alterparam vrf/vrf2 + reset) over DRIVELIST 0.010/0.014/0.020/0.028/0.040/0.056/0.080 V peak per tone (Pin -36.02 to -17.96 dBm), reading the IF-fundamental, both IM3 sidebands and the LO-leak bin at every step and echoing one SWEEPPOINT row (plus adjacent-pair LOCALSLOPE rows) per step into the corner log -- the shown slope region spec/porting-plan.md S4.1 requires for any real IIP3 claim.

Why swept (issue #165): the pre-#165 bench read IIP3 from ONE drive point (vrf=10 mV, Pin=-36.02 dBm), and once the issue-#135 exactly-coherent window removed the leakage that read turned out to sit ON the transient sampler's interpolation-error floor, not on a circuit IM3 product: along the sample-count axis pim3_dbm fell monotonically instead of converging (8192 samples: -104.7 dBm; 16384: -117.4; 32768: -124.2; 65536: -142.6 batch ngspice-46 vs -137.45 local ngspice-42), along the tolerance axis tightening reltol to 1e-6 moved it UP (-137 to -130 dBm), and across backends pim3/iip3 differed by 5.1/2.6 dB while pfund/lo_rf_leak agreed within 0.002 dB. A stronger single drive would have raised the product above the floor but could not show the 1:3 slope region S4.1 demands, so the bench now sweeps the drive and extrapolates only from the window the measured slopes verify.

Tracked IM3 sideband and fit window: the deck tracks the UPPER sideband 2*f2-f1-fLO = 1037.5 MHz. Measured on this placeholder (hbt_typ/27C/2.50V, this deck): the upper sideband is the DOMINANT pair member at every swept drive (-127.3 vs -137.5 dBm at 0.010 V up to -73.0 vs -78.0 at 0.080 V), so tracking it continues the pre-#165 'dominant sideband, conservative IIP3' convention; and its adjacent-pair local slope is the ideal ~3 (3.32 on the floor-grazing first pair, then 3.08/3.08/2.95/2.85/2.77), while the lower sideband's slope genuinely expands (1.88 floor pair, then 3.55/3.32/3.43/3.65/3.86) -- a real asymmetry of this single-ended topology, echoed per step (pim3_lo_962_dbm) as a diagnostic, not fitted. Fit window (the stated region IIP3 is extrapolated from): the five DRIVELIST steps 0.014/0.020/0.028/0.040/0.056 V (Pin -33.10 to -21.06 dBm). Excluded a priori: the lowest step 0.010 V -- its LOCALSLOPE pair reads 3.32 with the lower sideband at 1.88, the signature of the sampler floor grazing the product exactly where the pre-#165 single point sat -- and the highest step 0.080 V, where the tracked slope has departed furthest from 3 (2.77) and the fundamental shows its first expansion (1.0063): the compression probe, held out of the fit by construction. The deck least-squares-fits Pfund_dBm and the tracked Pim3_dBm vs Pin_dBm over the window (FITPOINT rows) and intersects the two lines; slope_fund_db_per_db (0.9..1.1) and slope_im3_db_per_db (2.7..3.3) are checked at every PVT point and fit_n pins the window length, so a window that quietly contained a compressed, expanded or floor-contaminated point fails the bench instead of publishing a fake IIP3.

One-tone floor control (issue #165): after the sweep the deck re-runs the SAME window with the second tone zeroed (alterparam vrf2 = 0) at the TOP-OF-FIT drive 0.056 V and reads the SAME tracked 1037.5 MHz bin -- a product-free bin holding only transient-sampler interpolation error and spurious content. pim3_floor_1tone_dbm is that read; pim3_fit_margin_db = pim3_dbm - pim3_floor_1tone_dbm at the same drive is the measured 'IM3 above floor' distance, checked >= 20 dB at every PVT point. The control runs at the top of the fit window because the margin there is the smallest the extrapolation relies on. Floor scaling note: the floor is NOT drive-independent -- the one-tone read at the top-of-fit drive (-131.8 dBm at 1037.5 MHz, nominal corner) sits ~5.6 dB above the pre-#165 10 mV floor read at the same bin family, so quoting only the old 10 mV floor would overstate today's margin.

Headline-point convention (changed with the method, issue #165): the single-number figures pin_dbm, pfund_dbm, pim3_dbm, conversion_gain_db, conv_gain_voltage_secondary_db and lo_rf_leak_dbm are read at the TOP-OF-FIT drive step (0.056 V, Pin -21.06 dBm) -- the most demanding point the linear model is asked to describe -- not at the pre-#165 fixed 10 mV. The full swept curve lives in each corner's log (SWEEPPOINT/LOCALSLOPE/FITPOINT/FLOORCONTROL/FIT rows); the pre-#165 10 mV figures remain in records 20260912-034727-9204518 and 20261011-225017-787dc96 under their own method statements, and are not comparable point-for-point with this bench's headline numbers.

Power-of-two sample count (issue #135): different ngspice builds handle a non-power-of-two `fft` input differently (this host's zero-pad, the batch fleet's ngspice-46 does not), so the window is exactly 65536 = 2^16 samples over an exactly-80-ns DFT record and both behaviours coincide ('zero padding: 0'; identical transform). Every transient in the swept deck logs its own 'FFT: ... input length ...' banner, so each SWEEPPOINT row is disclosable down to the producing transform; until 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#3095 makes klt disclose the runner's FFT build in the report, those banner lines are the disclosure.

Convergence study (issue #165 acceptance; hbt_typ/27C/2.50V, local ngspice-42, tracked 1037.5 MHz bin at the top-of-fit drive 0.056 V; produced by --no-write single-point runs of a scratch study variant of this deck -- one harness invocation per reltol rung, sample-count rungs unrolled inside the deck, no local loops; per-rung windows endpoint-aligned, tstop = 20n + (N-1)*tstep, the issue-#135 construction, so every valid rung's saved grid is exactly N uniform samples and the fft is coherent with zero padding): pim3_dbm by sample count N at default tolerances: 8192: -76.51; 16384: -79.90; 32768: -77.94; 65536: -81.61; 131072: -81.63; 262144: -81.63. The coarse-grid reads sit 2-5 dB HIGH (interpolation floor above the product; the rung's one-tone floor column: -116.3/-119.2/-118.8/-131.8/-134.2/-134.4 dBm) and bounce non-monotonically; from N=65536 the read is converged: within 0.03 dB of the 262144-sample asymptote. STATED BOUND: for N >= 65536 and reltol in {default(1e-3), 1e-4, 1e-5}, pim3_dbm stays within 0.2 dB of -81.63 (observed -81.61/-81.63/-81.63 default; -81.47/-81.64/-81.64 at 1e-4; -81.81/-81.65/-81.69 at 1e-5); pfund_dbm (the coherence canary) stays within 0.001 dB of -31.7905 across the same cells; the one-tone floor at those cells is -130.6 to -134.7 dBm, so the read carries a >= 50 dB floor margin. Tolerance mechanism (replaces the pre-#165 tolerance datum): ngspice saves its internal timepoints -- tstep is only the step CEILING -- so tightening reltol past the point where the integrator wants steps finer than tstep makes the saved stream non-uniform and the padded fft non-coherent; measured: reltol=1e-6 gives 65817 data rows for the 65536 grid, and every such cell reads garbage (e.g. the tracked bin at -56 dBm with the canary off by -4.4 dB). The pre-#165 datum 'reltol 1e-6 moved pim3 up from -137 to -130' was this padding leakage, not a floor shift. Valid cells are exactly those whose canary holds; at coarse N the uniformity boundary tightens (at reltol=1e-5 the 32768 rung is already non-uniform), so the table quotes only cells with a holding canary.

Tolerance axis at the FIT WINDOW's low end (2026-10-12 probe, hbt_typ/27C/2.50V, local ngspice-42, .options reltol=1e-5 deck variant, --no-write): the convergence bound above was measured at the TOP-OF-FIT read; the window's LOW-drive IM3 points are tolerance-fragile. reltol 1e-5 (uniform 65536-row grids, pfund canary holding to 0.001 dB) moved the per-point pim3_dbm UP: -117.611 -> -112.458 (+5.2 dB at 0.014 V), -108.070 -> -105.582, -99.080 -> -97.935, -89.929 -> -89.837, -81.607 -> -81.815 (top-of-fit -0.21 dB) -- and the fitted IM3 line flattened to slope 2.559, FAILING the bench's own 2.7..3.3 region gate. The low end does NOT converge along the tolerance axis within feasible tolerance; the 1:3 region the default-tolerance bench fits is partly tolerance-shaped; and the stated 0.2 dB bound (like the sample-count study's) is evidenced for the top-of-fit read only. Default reltol is retained as the bench's stated operating point -- it is the setting whose sample-count convergence IS shown and whose slope gate holds -- and an extrapolated IIP3 from this bench inherits the fragility; see the cross-backend note.

Cross-backend status (issue #165 acceptance): the 27-point PVT grid ran as THREE klt sim batch requests (one per supply, 9 process x temperature corners each; --runner-version-check warn --no-stage-models --no-write, 2026-10-12) on the fleet runner (klt 0.5.0, ngspice-46, runner-image models). The recording path stays blocked by the runner/client skew -- the 0.5.0 runner refuses the 0.7.0 client outright, with warn it ignores staged model inputs (2026-10-11: 'model library not found'), and the harness refuses to record unstaged-model runs -- so the grid's numbers are quoted here and in this bench's local record, not archived as corner logs; two earlier full-grid submits the same morning were rejected at BATCH_MAX_CONCURRENT_INSTANCES=8 (capacity; reported per the no-local-fallback rule, nothing run locally as a substitute). Results: all 27 corners simulated; the one-tone floor margin holds >= 50 dB at every corner (50.2..80.9 dB); the slope gates PASS at 21/27 corners and FAIL at 6 (hbt_typ & hbt_bcs at 125 C at 2.25/2.50 V, hbt_bcs/125 C at 2.75 V, hbt_wcs/-40 C at 2.25 V) -- at those corners the STATIC drive window contains no valid 1:3 region (hot corners compress inside it: slope_fund 0.52..0.76, slope_im3 1.79..4.42), no IIP3 is published there, and that is the gate working, not a circuit result; a per-corner-adaptive window is follow-up work. Nominal-corner backend comparison (hbt_typ/27C/2.50V; local = this host, ngspice-42, pinned PDK; batch = fleet runner, ngspice-46, runner-image models): pfund_dbm agrees to 0.0014 dB at every fit point and lo_rf_leak_dbm to 0.0002 dB; pim3_dbm at the top-of-fit drive is -81.607 local vs -81.507 batch = 0.0998 dB, WITHIN the issue-#135 0.1 dB criterion; the per-point pim3 agreement degrades toward the window's low end (0.0998 / 0.187 / 0.348 / 0.685 / 1.375 dB from 0.056 V down to 0.014 V); iip3_dbm (free two-line intersection) is +3.770 local vs +5.134 batch = 1.365 dB, NOT within the criterion: the intersection amplifies the low-end inter-build IM3 scatter ~15x across the ~31 dB extrapolation (slope-constrained estimators -- a slope-3 line through the window centroid, or the per-point Pfund+(Pfund-Pim3)/2 mean -- carry half the mean scatter, ~0.27 dB, still over 0.1). Verdict on the issue's 0.1 dB backend criterion at hbt_typ/27C/2.50V: MET for pim3_dbm, NOT met for iip3_dbm -- the extrapolated figure is build-sensitive at the bench's stated tolerance because the two builds agree the IM3 line's slope only to ~0.10 (2.996 vs 2.894) and the free intersection rotates with it; an honest iip3 backend bound for this bench is ~1.4 dB (free intersection) until the low-drive IM3 reads are tolerance-converged, which the reltol=1e-5 probe above shows tolerance alone does not deliver.

ngspice control-language constraints this deck works within (verified by probes on ngspice-42, 2026-10-12): solver tolerances CANNOT be changed from the control language (`option` inside .control is a silent no-op -- a numdgt probe showed no effect), so the tolerance axis of any convergence study needs separate deck variants, i.e. separate runs; `set var value` (space form) stores the string 'TRUE' rather than the number -- only the `set var=value` equals form is usable for numeric state; `$&name` resolves vectors only, `$name` set-variables only; `tran` arguments must be literals (a `$vector` tstep silently runs ngspice defaults). The deck therefore uses foreach + alterparam + reset + equals-form string accumulators for its in-deck least-squares fit. This is a pure ngspice gap, not a klayout-tools one; the klt-side workflow gap (a klt sim request expresses only PVT corner axes, so a swept bench must bake its drive loop into the deck and split tolerance studies across runs) was filed generically at 2AMLogic/klayout-tools.

dBm convention: Pin_dBm uses the standard available-power formula for a Thevenin source with series Z0 (V_peak^2/(8*Z0)); Pfund_dBm/Pim3_dBm/lo_rf_leak_dbm use V_peak^2/(2*Z0) at the (unterminated) output/RF-port node, i.e. Z0=50 ohm is a REPORTING reference only, not an assertion that the output is impedance-matched. Every dBc-difference term (conversion_gain_db; the IIP3 intersection is entirely in dBm-vs-dBm space) is insensitive to this approximation since all its terms use the identical conversion.

SSB noise figure: NOT SIMULATED. ngspice has no periodic-steady-state/periodic-noise (pnoise) analysis, so there is no valid way to linearize noise about this mixer's LO-pumped, time-varying operating point with a plain `.noise` analysis (which is only valid around a fixed DC bias point). spec/porting-plan.md S4.1 names three candidate routes for this (a transient-noise-source simulation; a manual per-LO-harmonic-sideband `.noise` sum; or an explicit 'not measurable in this flow' honest record) -- this bench takes the third. This is a real ngspice/general-SPICE tooling gap, not a klayout-tools gap -- klayout-tools does no simulation and is not invoked anywhere in this bench.

LO-to-RF leakage and the mismatch corners: spec/target-spec.md's verification-corners table calls for evaluating row 15 (LO leakage) against the HBT mismatch corner cards (hbt_typ_mismatch/hbt_bcs_mismatch/hbt_wcs_mismatch), since leakage is fundamentally a differential-pair symmetry effect in a balanced (Gilbert-cell) topology. This placeholder is SINGLE-ENDED -- there is no differential pair for a mismatch corner to unbalance -- so that guidance does not map onto this circuit; lo_rf_leak_dbm here is swept only against the plain (non-mismatch) hbt corner set, and read at every drive step (headline value: top-of-fit step; measured drive-independent here to ~0.001 dB across the sweep, as expected -- leakage is LO-driven, not RF-driven). Revisit once a real, likely balanced, topology exists.

No PDK inductor model exists for SG13G2 (confirmed absent in IHP-Open-PDK -- see sg13g2-vco's known_model_gaps note, restated in sim/README.md, and independently re-confirmed in spec/porting-plan.md S4.2). This fixture avoids the gap entirely: no inductor of any kind appears anywhere in the circuit -- RF/LO ports are resistive-source, capacitively-coupled, and the collector load and base bias path are plain resistors.

PLACEHOLDER CIRCUIT: single-ended, single-transistor active mixer (RF and LO summed at one npn13G2 base, Nx=4), not the double-balanced Gilbert-cell topology row 9's DRAFT target assumes. No spec row is claimed by this bench (issue #165 acceptance criterion); iip3_dbm here is a placeholder-circuit methodology number only.
